currencyNote: Importance 1–5 and optional hard line on every answered item.

sections.title: Marriage & commitment
sections.intro: What marriage means to you—commitment, decisions, openness, and priority.

sections.title: Children & parenting
sections.intro: Whether you want children, when, how many, and how you'd raise them.

sections.title: Money
sections.intro: Money disagreements are rarely just about dollars. These questions compare how you expect earning, spending, saving, debt, and generosity to work.

sections.title: Faith & values
sections.intro: Faith, spiritual practice, moral frameworks, and how much shared belief matters.

sections.title: Sex & affection
sections.intro: These questions are private. Their purpose is not to define a “normal” relationship. They identify whether your expectations differ.

sections.title: Communication & conflict
sections.intro: How you want to fight, apologize, cool down, and ask for help.

sections.title: Family & boundaries
sections.intro: In-laws, holidays, caregiving, friendships, and where the marriage sits relative to family.

sections.title: Career & ambition
sections.intro: Work identity, relocation, hours, risk, and income versus time.

sections.title: Home & lifestyle
sections.intro: Where you live, how you live, pets, travel, and the feel of home.

sections.title: Roles & responsibilities
sections.intro: Who does what—chores, childcare, money admin, and mental load.

sections.title: Health & habits
sections.intro: Substances, health, sleep, and habits that affect a shared life.

sections.title: Future & adversity
sections.intro: Marriage includes situations neither person can predict. These questions explore expectations about how you would face them.
